# casdoor_server (Resource)

Manages a Casdoor server, an MCP server whose tools are made available through Casdoor.

Only the attributes set in the configuration are written to Casdoor. The other fields of the object, including the ones not listed here, keep their current values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "casdoor_server" "tools" {
  owner        = casdoor_organization.acme.name
  name         = "tools"
  display_name = "Acme tools"
  url          = "https://mcp.acme.example.com/mcp"
  token        = var.mcp_token
  application  = casdoor_application.portal.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the server, unique within its owner.
- `owner` (String) The organization that the object belongs to.

### Optional

- `application` (String) The application of the server.
- `display_name` (String) The display name.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token used to call the MCP server.
- `url` (String) The URL of the MCP server.

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) The time when the server was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of the server in the `owner/name` format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the organization and the name.
terraform import casdoor_server.example <organization>/<name>
```
